The graphs of the functions $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ are given above. Find ${q}^{′}(-1)$ where $q(x)=f(x)-g(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
The addition and constant multiple rules for derivatives give

$$
{q}^{′}(x)={f}^{′}(x)-{g}^{′}(x).
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{q}^{′}(-1)={f}^{′}(-1)-{g}^{′}(-1).
$$

Also, notice that $x=-1$ corresponds to 

- the interval $x\in (-2,0)$ for the function $f,$ and

- the interval $x\in (-2,0)$ for the function $g,$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14193775/assets/244c8f29305d462ad11eabd50b9e55ae6b1de5d168d64768ed522a915aa1f283.png)

- The slope of $y=f(x)$ is constant on $x\in (-2,0)$ and equals

$$
\frac{Δf}{Δx}=\frac{3-1}{0-(-2)}=1.
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{′}(-1)=1.$

- The slope of $y=g(x)$ is constant on $x\in (-2,0)$ and equals

$$
\frac{Δg}{Δx}=\frac{(-3)-1}{0-(-2)}=-2.
$$

Therefore, ${g}^{′}(-1)=-2.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}^{′}(-1) & ={f}^{′}(-1)-{g}^{′}(-1) \\  & =1-(-2) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

The graphs of the functions $y=f(x)$ and $y=h(x)$ are given above. Find ${p}^{′}(-2)$ where $p(x)=f(x)h(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
The product rule for derivatives gives

$$
{p}^{′}(x)={f}^{′}(x)\cdot h(x)+f(x)\cdot {h}^{′}(x).
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{p}^{′}(-2)={f}^{′}(-2)\cdot h(-2)+f(-2)\cdot {h}^{′}(-2).
$$

From the graphs above, we obtain that $f(-2)=2$ and $h(-2)=-2.$

Additionally,

- The slope of $f(x)$ on $x\in (-3,0)$ equals $-1.$ So, ${f}^{′}(-2)=-1.$

- The slope of $h(x)$ on $x\in (-2.5,0)$ equals $2.$ So, ${h}^{′}(-2)=2.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{′}(-2) & ={f}^{′}(-2)\cdot h(-2)+f(-2)\cdot {h}^{′}(-2) \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-2)+2\cdot 2 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

The graphs of the functions $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ are given above. Find ${h}^{′}(-1.5)$ where $h(x)=f(x)g(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
The product rule for derivatives gives

$$
{h}^{′}(x)={f}^{′}(x)\cdot g(x)+f(x)\cdot {g}^{′}(x).
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(-1.5)={f}^{′}(-1.5)\cdot g(-1.5)+f(-1.5)\cdot {g}^{′}(-1.5).
$$

From the graphs above, we obtain that $f(-1.5)=-0.5$ and $g(-1.5)=-0.5.$

Additionally:

- The slope of $f(x)$ on $x\in (-2.5,0)$ equals $1.$ So, ${f}^{′}(-1.5)=1.$

- The slope of $g(x)$ on $x\in (-3,-0.5)$ equals $0.$ So, ${g}^{′}(-1.5)=0.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(-1.5) & ={f}^{′}(-1.5)\cdot g(-1.5)+f(-1.5)\cdot {g}^{′}(-1.5) \\  & =1\cdot (-0.5)+(-0.5)\cdot 0 \\  & =-0.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Given the plots of $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ above, find ${h}^{′}(1)$ where $h(x)=\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}.$

${h}^{′}(1)=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The quotient rule for derivatives gives

$$
{h}^{′}(x)=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)\cdot g(x)-f(x)\cdot {g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(1)=\frac{{f}^{′}(1)\cdot g(1)-f(1)\cdot {g}^{′}(1)}{(g(1))^{2}}.
$$

From the graphs above, we obtain that $f(1)=2$ and $g(1)=-1.$

Additionally:

- The slope of $f(x)$ on $x\in (-1,2.5)$ equals $1.$ So, ${f}^{′}(1)=1.$

- The slope of $g(x)$ on $x\in (0,2)$ equals $-2.$ So, ${g}^{′}(1)=-2.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(1) & =\frac{{f}^{′}(1)\cdot g(1)-f(1)\cdot {g}^{′}(1)}{(g(1))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot (-1)-2\cdot (-2)}{(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3}{1} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
